caption: The drawing depicts a single earthenware vessel that is brown in color with darker shading and highlights to convey its rounded, slightly bulbous shape. The vessel features an outwardly flared rim at the top, a curved body that narrows slightly toward the base, and lacks visible handles or decoration aside from an inscription impressed horizontally into its upper third. The inscription reads “309 PAUL CUSHMAN’S STONEWARE FACTORY. 1809,” which is also reproduced in a horizontal strip below the image of the vessel. The drawing is rendered on a cream-colored background and is contained within a rectangular border. The artist’s signature, “N. Amanita,” appears in the bottom right corner outside the border.
title: Stoneware Jar
cluster: #19 — Ceramic Arts: Pottery, Stoneware, and Porcelain
